question: which axis actually causes the serovar caller to abstain?
supersedes: the 2026-09-04 claim that phase-2 flagellin handling is this cell's single largest defect -- the COUNT of empty-H2 formulas was right, the causal attribution was not
why: the largest cause is `O_antigen_unresolved` at 21 of 59 (35.6%); the phase-2-reachable bucket is 13 (22.0%). The O:H1-unique fallback recovers 0 formulas, so its headroom is zero -- do not build it.
honest_limits: One cohort (N=200, reference-lab-filtered) and one antigen DB build. The cause mix would differ with a different O-antigen allele set.
This partitions by the FIRST failing axis. A formula can be wrong on more than one axis; the counts are of first-failure, not of independent defects.
It measures WHY the caller abstains, NOT whether a resolved call would be correct -- abstention and error are different failures and are counted separately throughout.
The O-antigen bucket is the largest but its fix is DB coverage (data engineering on the wzx/wzy allele set), not a code change -- sized here, not attempted.
